S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

symptom.disease_info: Acute Stress Disorder (ASD) is a time-limited trauma- and stressor-related condition that develops within days of exposure to an event involving actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violation, either directly, as a witness, or through close association. It is characterized by a cluster of intrusion, negative mood, dissociation, avoidance, and arousal symptoms lasting from 3 days to 1 month after the traumatic event, with clear associated functional impairment. Clinically, patients often present with marked distress and sudden changes in behavior or functioning shortly after the trauma, sometimes with dissociative experiences or pronounced hyperarousal. ASD is distinguished from posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) primarily by its shorter duration and earlier onset; persistent symptoms beyond one month raise concern for progression to PTSD or other comorbid conditions such as depression or substance use disorders.

patient.stressor: Mario had been helping coordinate a small cultural booth at a downtown Colorado Springs street fair when a car suddenly plowed through a barricade, striking several pedestrians just a few yards from where he was arranging decorations. He watched one of the senior-center volunteers he knew well get hit and thrown to the pavement, and spent the next several minutes trying to follow shouted instructions from first responders while the scene was chaotic, bloody, and confusing. In the days that followed, his normally busy routine of gardening, art classes, and senior-center activities fell apart as he found himself unable to relax at home or return to the plaza, and even routine errands along busy streets became overwhelming enough that he began canceling commitments. When church friends noticed he had stopped coming to Mass and to the hiking group and he admitted he was "jumping out of his skin" at every small noise and feeling unsafe leaving his apartment, his parish priest and a neighbor from the senior center urged him to see a mental health professional through the clinic that partners with the parish.
patient.chief_complaint: “Ever since that car drove into the crowd, even little sounds make me feel like I’m back there and I jump out of my chair or drop things.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: At night I lie there staring at the ceiling for hours, and when I do finally nod off I jerk awake over and over with my heart racing and those street fair images in my head, so I never feel like I’ve really slept even if the clock says I have.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: All week it’s like a film stuck on repeat in my mind—one second I’m washing dishes or trying to read the paper, and the next I’m seeing that car jump the curb and my friend’s body flying and the blood on the pavement, so real I have to grip the counter to steady myself.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I’ve been turning down rides past downtown, skipping the senior center and even Mass because just thinking about being near a busy street or a crowd makes my chest tighten and I push the whole thing out of my mind as fast as I can.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I can remember setting up the booth and then suddenly I’m holding someone’s hand on the ground, but there are big blank spots in between, like I can’t piece together how I got from one moment to the next no matter how hard I try.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: Since the accident I snap at people over nothing—my neighbor knocked to bring me soup and I barked at her to stop banging on my door, and I’ve caught myself cursing at the TV when a car commercial comes on, which isn’t like me at all.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.
S080.manifestation: Now even when a cabinet door closes a little hard or a motorcycle goes by outside, I jump out of my chair like a bomb went off, my whole body shaking and my heart pounding so hard it takes several minutes for me to calm down.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: In just this past week I’ve stopped going to the senior center, church, and my art class, and even put off grocery shopping because I feel too on edge and shaken to leave my apartment or focus on anything the way I used to.
add_requirements.duration: All of this started in the days right after the car drove into the crowd at the street fair and has been going on for about a week now.
